## Dieses Dokument

- Titel: Brief von Lotte Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred Altmann [19. November 1940], SZ-AAL/B1.64
- Signatur: SZ-AAL/B1.64
- Datum: 19.11.1940
- Objekttyp: Brief
- Umfang: 3 Scans

pages.transcription:
Rio, 19.11.40
Dear Hanna & Manfred, My sister-in-law's letter
about reading Eva's letter where she says that she did
not like it in her house, will have reached you be-
fore this one and I hope you don't take it seriously.
It is a stupid incident but without importance and it shows Eva's
childishness that she gave this letter - yes! - to my sister-in-law to
post it. The important thing is that she writes to you regularly,
for Salmon's seem to be in that respect like all our American
friends none of whom writes us a word, although definitely people like
Huebsch and Rose are good friends. They have not yet realised what letters
can mean to those far away. To me letters mean [?] and so please write, write many and long letters until finally the
personal contact can be reestablished. Kindest regards and best love
Lotte

Dear A. & M. we cannot tell you anything about Eva, as she did not
write to us - I have the feeling that the Helaus[?] like to keep her for
themselves and do nothing to keep her in touch with her family
Eva will perhaps have to fight to get her back from her new parents.
Anyhow we hope to see her in February. For the moment we have but
one desire: To sit quietly and not to move. I have done enough with
travelling by air and auto and trains and hydroplanes in those 16
days - more than another in a lifetime and the idea to travel
14 days to New York is for the moment a ghastly one for me. I am
very worried about Manfred. I do not understand why he must
just now start a new profession as a Xray specialist - after
the war his practice will flourish again and he would better do
to take a rest. Dont think too much about the future and remem-
ber always that you have a child who wants you. Dont worry
about money, you should know already that one of the very few
pleasures I have now{left} is to know that you have not to think about
and may freely and largely dispose of all I have - we have a
duty one against the other in such times. I told you that I had
to give ten lectures instead of four and am invited to give
more in Danish and in all possible countries of South America
- so we have at least something useful to do and I am glad that
I am physically able to assist stand the great
strain. Ever yours Stefan Zweig
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief auf Briefpapier der 'Editora Guanabara'. Violette Tinte. Am linken Rand vertikal geschriebener Text: 'I am physically able to assist stand the great strain. Ever yours Stefan Zweig'. Der Text ist gut lesbar.

result.confidence_notes: Der Text ist sehr gut lesbar, trotz der handschriftlichen Natur und der Randnotizen. Die wenigen unsicheren Stellen sind als [?] markiert.
